messages:
priya: Heads up — since ~08:35 we've seen recurring sawtooth latency spikes on gRPC bidi streams to model-service via egress-proxy-2 in eu-west-3. Throughput is steady but p95 token latency jumps ~700-900ms then recovers. Anyone else seeing this pattern?

dan: Saw the alert. Graphs looked periodic (~30-45s). Could be connection-level write stalls or flow-control thrash. Which load balancer sits in front?

priya: @dan it's the internal edge-alb-v2 feeding egress-proxy-2 -> worker pool. Proxy logs show repeated "write_blocked" messages during spikes.

sergei: Can you paste a short log snippet and a tcpdump? Also check NAT ephemeral port counts in the subnet.

priya: Log snippet:

[2026-03-18T08:35:12Z] WARN proxy write_blocked fd=24 bytes=0 reason=EAGAIN wait_ms=30
[2026-03-18T08:35:42Z] WARN proxy write_blocked fd=24 bytes=0 reason=EAGAIN wait_ms=28
[2026-03-18T08:36:14Z] WARN proxy write_blocked fd=24 bytes=0 reason=EAGAIN wait_ms=33

tanya: That looks like upstream write backpressure on the socket. Did we roll any H2/window-change patches recently? @alex rolled anything last night?

alex: Pushed a small window-clamp fix to edge-alb-canary last night but didn't touch egress-proxy builds. egress-proxy-2 still on v2026.03.10.

dan: Two hypotheses: 1) ALB is coalescing frames and causing sporadic write stalls, 2) kernel/GSO/tx offload interplay on proxy causing bursts. Also check for FIN_WAIT or repeated stream resets.

priya: Quick checks: ESTAB sockets ~920 (not saturated). But I do see bursts of FIN_WAIT around the same timestamps as spikes. Ran a tcpdump 20s capture, saw repeated WINDOW_UPDATE frames followed by small data frames. Snippet:

08:35:12.123 IP proxy -> alb: H2 SETTINGS
08:35:12.124 IP alb -> proxy: WINDOW_UPDATE stream 0 +16384
08:35:42.118 IP proxy -> alb: DATA length=512 flags=
08:35:42.119 IP alb -> proxy: RST_STREAM stream=7

sergei: RST_STREAM + WINDOW_UPDATE churn suggests ALB or an intermediary is unhappy with long-lived streams. Could be LB healthchecks or idle timeouts interfering with streaming windows.

alex: I'll schedule a canary of the newer proxy runtime on egress-proxy-2 to see if write_blocked changes. infra-bot: schedule deploy egress-proxy-2 -> edge-proxy:v2026.03.17-canary

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: egress-proxy-2 will receive edge-proxy:v2026.03.17-canary in 2m (rolling, 1 instance).

tanya: Also we should reproduce bypassing the ALB: point traffic directly at node port IP and run grpcurl to verify if LB is the root cause. If bypass improves smoothing then open ticket with cloud LB.

priya: Canary rolled a minute ago. Early metrics show p95 improved ~120ms baseline but the sawtooth spikes are still visible at lower amplitude. Running controlled grpcurl stream tests bypassing ALB now.

dan: If bypass stabilizes streams, escalate to cloud support and include H2 SETTINGS/WINDOW_UPDATE traces + packet captures. Also check kernel tx offload toggles on proxy nodes (GSO/TCP segmentation) — those have caused weird bursts before.

priya: Bypass test results: direct-to-node stream has far fewer spikes, p95 stable. With ALB in path we reproduce spikes reliably.

sergei: OK plan: 1) keep canary on proxy for now, 2) run 15m controlled test with and without ALB and collect full H2 trace, 3) gather ALB metrics (idle timeouts, keepalive resets), 4) file cloud LB ticket if ALB reproduces. Add rollback if p95 > 400ms for >5m.

alex: I'll put together an autoscript for rollback and grab a canary runbook.

priya: Thanks all — I'll drop full traces and the tcpdump here when ready. :thumbsup:
